title: Attractor-Vascular Coupling Theory: Formal Grounding and Empirical Validation for AAMI-Standard Cuffless Blood Pressure Estimation from Smartphone Photoplethysmography
abstract: arXiv:2605.10871v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: We present Attractor-Vascular Coupling Theory (AVCT), a theory-guided framework for deriving interpretable blood pressure (BP) predictors from photoplethysmography (PPG) attractor geometry. AVCT connects vascular dynamics, PPG observation, delay-coordinate reconstruction, and attractor descriptors within a unified framework for formulating testable hypotheses, without presupposing the physiological sufficiency of a particular low-dimensional feature set. We evaluate a LightGBM-based estimator using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOSO-CV) across two complementary experimental settings. Experiment 1 comprises 46 ICU/surgical subjects from BIDMC and VitalDB, with ECG, PPG, and repeated reference BP measurements. The calibrated full model achieves systolic/diastolic BP (SBP/DBP) mean absolute errors (MAEs) of 2.05/1.67 mmHg, compared with 2.02/1.63 mmHg for the PPG-attractor-only model. translated_title: 吸引子-血管耦合理论：基于智能手机光电容积脉搏波图的无袖带血压估计的形式化基础与实证验证（符合AAMI标准）
translated_abstract: 我们提出了吸引子-血管耦合理论（AVCT），这是一个理论指导的框架，用于从光电容积脉搏波图（PPG）吸引子几何结构中推导可解释的血压（BP）预测因子。AVCT将血管动力学、PPG观测、延迟坐标重构和吸引子描述符连接在一个统一的框架内，以形成可检验的假设，而不预先假定某个特定低维特征集具有生理充分性。我们在两个互补的实验设置下，使用留一受试者交叉验证（LOSO-CV）评估了基于LightGBM的血压估计器。实验1包含来自BIDMC和VitalDB数据库的46名ICU/手术受试者，拥有心电图（ECG）、PPG及重复的参考血压测量数据。校准后的完整模型实现了收缩压/舒张压（SBP/DBP）平均绝对误差（MAE）为2.05/1.67 mmHg，而仅使用PPG吸引子特征的模型则为2.02/1.63 mmHg。实验2包括217名动态（门诊）……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出吸引子-血管耦合理论（AVCT），从PPG吸引子几何结构出发构建可解释的血压预测框架，实现了符合AAMI标准的智能手机无袖带血压估计，校准后收缩压/舒张压平均绝对误差仅2.05/1.67 mmHg。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Attractor-Vascular Coupling Theory (AVCT), a theory-guided framework deriving interpretable blood pressure predictors from PPG attractor geometry, achieving AAMI-standard smartphone cuffless blood pressure estimation with calibrated SBP/DBP mean absolute errors of only 2.05/1.67 mmHg.
